# The Night Parade

*Pages PDF 3-21*

_Along the Empire’s roads, the dead walk. Called from their slumber by a necromancer’s profane whispers, or buried where dark magic saturates the ground, these Undead march without rest, adding to their number with each hapless soul they cross. Whether such bands move with a purpose or wander aimlessly, they often find themselves the centre of folk tales.  Many a terrified tavern audience has gathered around the fire to hear stories of wild hunts, ghostly processions, and corpse-laden carts come to carry away the unwary._ 

_Of these, one story has risen to prominence. If you wander through the fertile lands between the Grey Mountains and the Reikwald Forest, listen always for the sounds of creaking wheels and a tolling bell. Do not wait to ask the carriage for a lift. Hide. Cover your ears. And whatever you do, do not follow where the bell leads. The Night Parade are calling._ 

The Night Parade are a band of wandering Undead, drawn together by the ancient Liche, Old Jasper. Setting out from the Grey Mountains when both moons shine as crescents, he leads his charges through the Vorbergland, calling the dead to him wherever they go. There appears to be little rhyme or reason to the Night Parade’s journeys. Yet, each time they are sighted, their numbers are sure to grow. 

## **Getting Started**
**The Night Parade** is a continuation in the series of supplements that started with the Forest Goblin **Cluster Eye Tribe** . However, where that supplement provided templates for tribal warbands, this supplement focuses on wandering groups of Undead. These may rise wherever magic is powerful or corrupted, even without a necromancer’s summons. Alongside full profiles of the Night Parade are templates to advance the basic Undead creatures found in the **Warhammer Fantasy Rulebook** ( **WFRP** , pages 327–30), turning them into Liche Corpsemasters, Liche Lords, Wights, Wight Champions, and Mass Grave Dead, as well as templates to raise mounts as Undead steeds. It also includes full rules and adventure hooks for Corpse Carts. These templates are intended to help bring more variety to your Undead encounters. The creatures presented in the **Warhammer Fantasy Rulebook** and the templates here are intended as a starting point — customise them however you see fit. 

To apply these templates, add or subtract the number of Advances from the creature’s base Characteristics, along with any Skills, Talents, or Trappings indicated. Some templates also include options for further customisation. For example, if you wish to make a skeletal Undead lord, apply the Wight Champion template to the Skeleton profile ( **WFRP** , page 327). These templates may also affect the creature’s Wounds, so be sure to recalculate these after adjusting the creature’s S, T, and WP according to the template. 

If you have never seen a pistoleer at work, I implore you to take some time and visit the Imperial Gunnery School. You will no doubt be impressed by what you see, and enjoy a rather more pleasant introduction to the art than I experienced. As it was, I barely registered the Zombie before Sovrissniz’s bullet cracked its skull like an egg. 

The Dwarf gunner seemed mighty pleased with her handiwork and, when the shock wore off, my companions and I were most complimentary (although Professor Pfaff grumbled a bit about the slight spattering of brain he received). Our guide, a rough-looking fellow named Arnholt, proved harder to impress. 

‘Stupid’ he cursed, kicking the corpse to the side. ‘What if there were more, eh? That cursed firearm will have alerted every wandering dead thing from here to the Grey Mountains!’ 

One does not insult a Dwarf lightly, and fisticuffs may have ensued had my companion Professor Gronighof not then offered Sovrissniz his flask of Bretonnian brandy in a toast. 

We had been travelling the Vorbergland for two days, an accident on the road to Bögenhafen and the subsequent loss of our carriage necessitating a detour south. I will admit, I had been quite enjoying our little walking tour, even though it meant enduring the constant arguments between Pfaff and our Eonir companion Kaia about proper flora and fauna nomenclature. After many weeks under the Reikwald’s close boughs, the Vorbergland’s open skies proved a welcome relief. 

However, the Zombie’s appearance hung a pall over the day, and when a moment later we heard something rustling in the underbrush, a chill terror settled upon me. Arnholt readied his axe. Sovrissniz prepared her second pistol. Meanwhile, Professor Pfaff and I took the chance to hide behind Gronighof, whose prowess in the university’s duelling club he is never shy to assure us of. 

Being prepared for any horror, the sharp, whispered ‘Pst!’ took us all by surprise. 

A grubby-faced vagrant stepped out, dressed in the rags of those who live their lives on the road. She gestured for us to follow, then dove back into the brush. 

We all stood there for some time, stunned. A second later, the woman reappeared. ‘Are you daft?’ she hissed. ‘Get off the road and follow me. The Night Parade are coming!’ 

Warning delivered, she disappeared again. 

I looked at my companions. They seemed as nonplussed as I. In the end, it was Kaia who took the initiative, pulling aside the tangled hedge to reveal a rough-beaten trail leading around a hillock. While she and Arnholt argued over our next move, I considered the woman’s words. 

The Night Parade was not a name I had come across in any of my own studies of the region’s history. Of course, given the apparent fear in her tone, they might well have been more the subject of folklore. 

I remembered reading in Maria Conte’s treatise upon the Vampire Wars ( _Children of the Night: The Fall of the Von Carsteins and the Nature of Those They Command_ ; University of Miragliano Press; 2406 IC) that the Undead, while usually a necromancer’s puppets, may also rise due to a natural suffusion of death magic. Lacking a creator’s purpose, they fall back upon bestial instincts, guarding their burial place or wandering in search of prey. Conte hypothesised this to be evidence that we sentient beings share a common ancestry with simple beasts, one which surfaces when death strips away our civility. This is, of course, a laughable notion, and I made sure to share it with my companions later. 

Though such Undead are rarely much of a threat, save to lone travellers, Conte  speculated that many local superstitions could be ascribed to them, as peasants look for some semblance of purpose in deaths caused by their random perambulations. The prospect of bearing witness to such a case banished all caution, and I eagerly followed the vagrant, much to Arnholt’s shouted frustrations. 

The path led to a hollow in the hillside, stinking of rancid smoke and slowly roasting rabbit. The woman who had accosted us sat inside, along with an equally ragged Halfling. They both kept a wary eye upon us, but shuffled over  to make room. 

‘These fine gents were stirring up the dead,’ the woman hissed. ‘What with dark comin’ on, I thought it best they hide here.’ 

Arnholt scoffed at this. ‘Hide from the Night Parade? It’s just some corpses without the sense to know they’re dead. I put down dozens of them on this road.’ 

‘Aye, sir,’ the woman’s companion said. ‘But it’s a twin crescent night. Old Jasper will be abroad. You don’t want to cross paths with him and his.’ 

Arnholt choked back a laugh and stomped off in search of firewood. He appeared familiar with this Night Parade, but didn’t warrant it such hushed reverence. I, on the other hand, was already preparing parchment and quill. My companions seemed less thrilled by the company, but as twilight was quickly leaching colour from the world, and the two moons were indeed locking horns, this rough shelter seemed our best option for the evening. 

As Gronighof availed himself of our hosts’ meagre supper, I set to interrogating them about this Night Parade. At first, they proved reticent, nervously eying the shadows, but a few coins later, they were eager to share their stories. 

‘My cousin over towards Amchensee says he saw him once,’ the dirt-crusted Halfling began. He said some skeleton, dressed all in ribbons, turned up dancing round the cemetery. When the guard went to deal with it, it told them to bring out their dead. Then it hopped over the palisade wall.’ He clicked his fingers. ‘Sharp as you like.’ 

## ‘And That Was Old Jasper?’
‘Nah, I never said that, did I?’ The Halfling glanced at the rising moons and began snuffing out their meagre fire. ‘My cousin, he said he stayed up that night and he heard a bell passing outside. He crept to the window and opened the shutter, just an inch. And there he was.’ 

The Halfling shuddered. ‘He rode atop a cart, ‘cept weren’t no horses pullin’ it. A pair of dead folks hauled it along. Old Jasper, he were just this hooded figure driving them on with a whip. And inside the cart… Corpses. Piles and piles of corpses, all wailing and crying and reaching out between the boards. My cousin, well he were so afeared he let out a gasp. And that’s when Old Jasper looked at him! Next day, he were as dead as that rabbit.’ 

The cold night crept in, running its fingers up my spine. I busied myself trying to see where the story fit with Conte’s treatise. Carts filled with the Undead were common enough. She said they had even been weaponised, most notably by the infamous necromancer Vanhel, who first gave Sylvania that region’s sinister reputation. Something about these constructs strengthened his magic, invigorating the Zombies he raised. When he was defeated, they simply wandered off, disappearing into the Empire’s forests. Could the Night Parade be some remnant of that long-defeated enemy? 

The spell was broken, predictably enough, by Gronighof. ‘If your cousin died, how, by the leathern shaft of Sigmar’s hammer, did you hear of his story?’ 

‘Well, obviously he told me first,’ the Halfling snapped back. 

‘If this Old Jasper is so dangerous,’ Pfaff interjected, ‘why has no one dealt with him?’ He shot Gronighof a glare which had a lot to say about manners to hosts and blasphemy in particular. 

‘Ah, see, that’s the thing,’ the woman said. ‘They’ve tried. Plenty of times, they’ve tried. But he’s protected, see. They say a group of ancient warriors march with him. Skeletons whose eyes burn with silver fire.’ 

She looked around at us, eyes glittering in the fading embers. ‘They say he found them buried in one of the barrows hereabouts. Old warriors from before even Sigmar walked. They ain’t no normal shufflers. You try asking a soldier to stare death in the face like that for a week’s wages and all the horse bread they can choke on.’ 

While she was speaking, her hand went to a tattered ribbon hanging from her jerkin. Beneath the grime, I could just make out the colours of an Ubersreik regiment. 

Silence settled over the company. Outside, just beyond our noisome shelter, the wind began to pick up, rustling the dense undergrowth. I found my imagination populating the world beyond with a thousand, staring eyes. 

‘Pah! Call that a spook story, do you?’ Gronighof broke in. ‘That wouldn’t scare my daughter’s wet nurse! Here, let me tell you a tale I heard in Bretonnia about the ague-spreading cavalcade.’ 

To our hosts’ growing consternation, the night quickly devolved into a game of one-upmanship over who could tell the most frightening tale. Gronighof’s story featured a garishly covered wagon travelling through Bretonnia, draining the life from those cursed to follow it. Not to be outdone, Sovrissniz — shared a tale from the Undgrin Ankor that vast underground network connecting the Dwarf holds — about travellers who hear the muffled sounds of pickaxes coming closer and, upon snuffing out their lanterns, find themselves face to face with those who died there, perishing cold and alone in the dark. 

Oddly, this dispelled some of the tension that had fallen over us since the zombie’s first appearance, as though by telling these tales we were dragging it back into the realms of the fanciful. I am sure Conte would have been proud to observe her hypothesis on the origin of superstitions in play. 

I, for my part, withdrew to the hollow’s entrance to reflect upon what I had heard. Everything the vagrants told us about this Night Parade lined up with Conte’s observations on what she referred to as the ‘common forms’ of Undeath. — Certainly, there were stories of ancient Undead warriors — wights, as those who study such things call them serving evil spellcasters as bodyguards. 

This Old Jasper, though, was something less certain. He could, of course, be a simple Human practitioner of the necromantic arts, but from what I gathered, these stories went back quite some time. No mortal, not even one who deals in death, can extend their lives beyond that which the gods have allotted for them. Unless, of course, Old Jasper had become something else entirely. 

In her background to the Vampire Wars, Conte briefly touched upon ancient Nehekhara. In that place, she said, there had once been a priesthood who escaped the bonds of mortality, yet at the price of their humanity. Could this ‘Old Jasper’ be something similar? I believe Conte would have written more upon the subject, had she ever returned from her subsequent research trip to the region. 

I was so wrapped up in my thoughts I did not notice Kaia join me. I jumped to find her so close, and began babbling some half-formed apology, only for her to shush me as though I were a misbehaving student. It was then I noticed she wasn’t looking at me, but out into the night beyond. 

It is very hard to tell what an Elf is feeling. They keep their emotions locked up tight behind those haughty features. However, I had by this point been travelling with the Eonir long enough to pick up some tells. Her jaw was taut, her eyes darted here and there, as though tracking movements I couldn’t follow in the gloom beyond. Then, mixed with the sighing of the wind, I heard the tolling of a distant bell. 

Behind us, the conversation died. Our hosts let out a whimper, and clutched one another tightly. I strained my hearing, trying to get some clue of the bell’s origin. And as I listened the low moaning of the wind transformed, becoming instead a chorus of voices. There were words in there, but either they were too far away to be heard clearly, or else they were in a language which skittered away from my understanding. It was like hearing the shape of words, stripped from their language. The voices and bell got louder. Down below, on the distant road, I heard the tramp-tramp of many feet, punctuated by the creaking of cart wheels. 

A hand took me by the shoulder, making me jump again. I looked back to find Pfaff, eyes wide, one hand gripping the hammer sigil he always wore around his neck. He gestured back away from the opening, and it was only then I understood we might truly be in danger. 

The realisation of how close we might be to the subjects of our stories… Well, it was exhilarating. And terrifying. Like a clammy hand squeezing tight around my chest. I allowed Pfaff to draw me back into the hollow, where we huddled together with Gronighof and our two hosts, their own eyes wide and shining in the meagre light of the twin moons. 

As the piteous cries grew louder, and the creaking wheels came closer, Sovrissniz moved to join Kaia in her vigil. Even in my not altogether lucid state, I was astonished to see her offer the Elf one of her precious pistols. The two of them kept watch for the rest of the night, while high above the twin moons grinned down into our shelter, leaving us feeling open and exposed to whatever lay beyond. 

Morning came far too slowly for my liking. Even as light filtered back into the world, I didn’t dare to move. Not until Kaia nodded that all was safe did I try to stand. 

The cold night had leached the strength from my limbs, and a feverish sweat clung to my skin. Looking at my companions, I was sure none of them had managed to sleep a wink either. We all stood, hollow-eyed and haggard by our night’s experience. 

We abandoned the camp in silence, packing up our belongings before making our way back to the road. The dirt track now bore the signs of heavy use; deep wheel ruts cut into the earth, surrounded by dragging footprints. Less wholesome remains littered the sides of the road, which I decided not to pay too close an eye to. 

We bade our hosts farewell, and resumed our journey towards Bögenhafen. Tired as I was, I was far more eager to see the back of these low scrublands, where all of a sudden I felt more exposed and alone than I ever had while travelling beneath the Reikwald’s dismal canopy. We never did see anything further of Arnholt, and left his payment waiting for him at the first inn we encountered. 

## **Undead Advancement Templates**
## **Mass Grave Dead**
Mass graves, charnel pits, ossuaries, and other forms of mass burial are common in the Old World. When the dead rise from such places, it is rarely as individuals. Instead, they come together as great, amorphous constructs, living piles of viscera and bone from which skulls chatter and limbs grasp. 

The following template can be applied to either the Zombie or Skeleton Characteristics. 

## **Liche Lord**
Should a Liche survive long enough to reclaim their mind, they become true masters of Undeath. Jealous and secretive, these entities hide themselves away in strongholds, growing in power until, at last, they are ready to take their rightful place as this world’s rulers. Where a Liche Lord walks, crops wither and Undead legions march to their whispered commands. 

Liche Lords use the basic Zombie Characteristics, but do not possess the _Construct_ Trait.

## **Liche Corpsemasters**
To become a Liche is the fate of any who plumbs necromancy’s secrets in an effort to avoid death. Their soul is bound to their body, escaping mortality’s grasp by trapping themselves inside their own decaying flesh. The process is traumatic. Most minds shatter at the horror of such an existence, causing the Liche to lose much of their previous power. Despite this, their will still burns strong, allowing them to command the lesser Undead and earning them the title ‘Corpsemaster’.

## **Wight**
The world is filled with ancient burial sites. _Dhar_ pools in such places, bathing the bones inside in its power. The resulting Undead are no mere Skeletons. Something of who they were clings to their remains, allowing them to fight with the skill they knew in life. Often, Wights form a necromancer’s dedicated Grave Guard, serving as loyal elites. However, sometimes a Wight will escape their tomb and begin following paths long overgrown. Lesser Undead gather to such creatures, drawn by the dark magic that clings to them still.

## **Wight Champion**

Chiefs from ancient times rise from their barrows, given life by Dark Magic and their singular sense of purpose. A world that has forgotten them. A world they must reconquer.

## **Undead Mounts**
A person’s mount may rise with them. Skeletons, Zombies, Wights, and Liches may take Ride (Rotting Mount) +20, or Ride (Skeletal Steed) +20 as additional Skills. Liches and Necromancers may also take Ride (Corpse Cart) +20. 

The following templates can be applied to any creature that might normally have the _Trained (Mount)_ Trait, whose Size Trait is _Large_ or smaller. Where a Characteristic reads ‘-1/2,’ that Trait is halved with the final value rounded down. Where it reads ‘-All,’ that Characteristic can no longer be used. 

## **Skeletal Steed**
Stipped of their flesh and risen from the grave to service once again, Skeletal Mounts are typically made from horses, but any suitable animal may be used by enterprising necromancers. Skeletal Mounts no longer have the _Flight_ Trait.

## **Without Rest**
The Night Parade are a wandering band of Undead who have haunted the lands by the Grey Mountains for countless decades. They follow the ancient Liche known as Old Jasper, who directs them from atop his Corpse Cart. He in turn is in thrall to a much darker presence, and it is by its command he is cursed to wander, collecting the Empire’s dead. 

When the twin moons both shine as crescents, a crack appears in the Grey Mountains’ foothills. Out of this rides Old Jasper, his Corpse Cart’s bell calling the dead to him wherever they lie. At his side marches a contingent of Wights, ancient warriors dead even before the time of Sigmar. Together, they follow the Empire’s winding roads, passing through towns and settlements, adding their dead to their number. 

When the Night Parade march, a herald appears ahead of them, announcing their presence and commanding villagers to bring out their dead. Should they not heed the Herald’s call, the Parade takes them by force. 

There are many types of dead in the Night Parade. Zombies make up their bulk, claimed from the meagre burial places which serve most small human settlements. To their number are added Skeletons, drawn from the battlefields never far beneath the Empire’s soil. Creatures from both forest and farm lumber along at their flanks, called by the Corpse Cart’s constant bell, while at the rear crawl Mass Grave Dead abominations, made from those denied the dignity of their own final resting place. 

The Night Parade are the dominant Undead in the Vorbergland. Most settlements have a story about them: some tale about a friend of a friend who disappeared after daring to peek out their window when the Night Parade  passed. They sweep other wandering Undead into their number, empty graves and plunder battlefields, before Jasper leads the motley procession back into the mountains. The Parade’s true master is a mystery, if indeed it even has one and Old Jasper is not simply mad. Of those dead taken into the foothills, nothing is seen again. 

## The Master in Shadows
There are many possibilities for the Night Parade’s true master. Perhaps Jasper serves the spirit of a once-great noble who sends him out from her ruined castle to gather up new members for her court. A Vampire from the Necrarch line might have need of such a figure, having Jasper fetch the raw materials needed for their magic. Given their proximity to the Grey Mountains, the Night Parade could be in service to the Great Enchanter, Drachenfels himself, allowing you to create an adventure featuring this classic villain (or a remnant of him). 

## **Disposition of the Night Parade**
This list represents the Night Parade at their full strength. Unlike living warbands, whose strength diminishes the longer they operate due to attrition, Undead grow in strength the longer they go unchecked. Once the Night Parade have reached something approaching the full complement listed here, they return to the Grey Mountains, unless something particularly tempting, such as a recent battlefield, comes to their attention. 

Unlike tribal warbands, the Undead have little in the way of an organised structure. They do not tend to maintain dedicated scouts or ambush parties. Instead, Old Jasper forms the Parade’s centre, and his paranoia means the stronger Undead are generally found closer to him, while the flanks and rear are more likely to be made up of stragglers and newcomers. The exact nature of their make-up depends on the type of dead the Night Parade have come across. 

## Insignia
Mheava’s Wights carry shields with the faded imprint of her insignia, a dead wolf bleeding from a spear wound. 

Tattered scraps of skin hang from Old Jasper’s Corpse Cart, covered in a spidery script glowing the colour of Morrslieb. 

## Battlecry
Jasper’s tolling bell. 

## Tactics
Depending on the Parade’s size, the Herald will go into settlements ahead of the main force. Should the Herald be killed, Jasper steers the Parade towards a safer target. His aim is to gather as many dead as possible. Places where the tally would go against him hold little interest. 

The full Night Parade consist of: 

- Mheava (Skeletal Steed-mounted Wight Champion) with two Skeleton cavalry (skeletal steed-mounted Skeletons), three Skeletons, and four Zombies, about a mile ahead of the main force. 

- Left flank lesser Undead, half a mile from Jasper, consisting of one Wight, two Dire Wolves, and seven Zombies. 

- Right flank lesser Undead, half a mile from Jasper, consisting of one Wight, four Skeletons, two Dire Wolves, and one Zombie Demigryph. 

- A command corps consisting of Old Jasper (Corpse Cart-mounted Liche), two Wights, two Skeletons, and four Zombies. 

When at full strength, the Night Parade rely on sheer numbers. The main force of lesser Undead march at the head, clearing the way for Jasper. 

He always makes burial places his priority, letting the Zombies and Skeletons stir chaos through a settlement while he directs his Corpse Cart to any graveyards or cemeteries there may be. If a settlement capitulates to the Night Parade, they will generally be left unmolested. The Night Parade pass through, taking the dead with them and leaving alone any living who stay indoors . 

When conflict is inevitable, the Night Parade wear their enemy down with a tide of lesser Undead, Zombiess and Skeletons growing in vitality as the Corpse Cart approaches. Unusually for a necromancer, Jasper prefers not to spend his human dead where possible, sending the less valuable Undead creatures and Mass Grave Dead ahead when a greater threat presents itself. 

- The rear, up to a mile from Jasper, consisting of The Herald (rotten steed-mounted Wight), five Zombies and The Charnel Chorus. 

## Uniform
The Night Parade wear whatever scraps still cling to their corpses. The exception is Mheava and her fellow Wights, all of whom wear wolf cloaks split in two along their length. 

At Ease: The Night Parade never stop moving and their paths are impossible to predict, unless one is aware of a recent bout of plague or a battle nearby. While on the move, the Parade spread out with Jasper at their centre. The further away they are from the Corpse Cart, the less control Jasper wields over the Undead, making their actions erratic. Adventurers are more likely to encounter these outlying stragglers than the Parade’s core itself, and might observe wandering Undead moving with more purpose than such creatures normally display. Combat and noise will draw other groups, but rarely attract Jasper’s attention, unless they come too close to the Parade’s centre. On such occasions, Mheava is sent to deal with the interloper. 

## **Old Asper J Liche Corpsemaster**
Little is known about Old Jasper, the shrouded figure who leads the Night Parade. He sits atop his Corpse Cart, little more than two silver eyes gleaming from within a rotting grey robe, urging his charges on in his endless search for fresh dead. Everywhere the Parade passes has its own story about him. 

According to one, Old Jasper was once a simple corpse collector tasked by Morr’s priesthood to gather those who fell to a plague known as the Crimson Jitters. Jasper took the job thinking Morr’s blessing would spare him. Slowly, though, red splotches blossomed across his skin and his muscles began to twitch. In anger, he stole the bodies away, selling them to physicians, wizards, and less savoury types. For this crime, Morr’s priests cursed him to existence without rest. Even to this day he  travels on, taking his revenge on Morr by stealing those in his care. 

Others say Old Jasper was once a necromancer who delved too deep into that forbidden practice. In his hubris, he attempted a spell far beyond his abilities, tearing his soul to shreds. Now he wanders the world searching for its scraps, the emptiness within him drawing the dead to his side. Another says he was a performer who mocked a mage of the Amethyst College. A cursed charlatan, a remnant of the Vampire Wars, the fallen apprentice of Frederick Vanhal; stories follow the Liche like flies. 

The truth, if there even is one, is impossible to tell for sure. It is doubtful whether even Old Jasper remembers. All he knows is that he has a purpose, a task he must fulfil or else wander forever. The dead he collects are the price he must pay. He has nearly gathered enough; he can feel it. Perhaps just one more march of the Night Parade…

## Old Jasper’s Corpse Cart
Old Jasper’s Corpse Cart follows all the rules for such constructs detailed on page 19 of this supplement. It has both the _Distracting_ and _Trained (Mount)_ optional Traits. 

## **Mheava Wight Champion**
Before Sigmar, the Old World was home to many warring human tribes. Great chieftains rose and fell, fighting Orcs, Beastmen, Dwarfs, Elves, and one another in an endless effort to claw out land for their own. At one point, the territories now known as the Vorbergland were ruled by the chieftain Mheava. Though a fearsome warrior in her own right, Mheava’s greatest strength came from her ability to forge allegiances. With the Dwarfs still reeling from their conflict with the Elves, Mheava turned to the Beastmen. The alliance was tentative — neither side ever trusted the other — but their combined strength gave them the means to stand against the Greenskins, forming an island against their tide. 

Soon, trade sprang up between the two peoples. The Beastmen turned over profits from their raids, or meat from their hunts, in return for arms and sacrifices. The Bray Shamans lent the humans their power, and soon Chaos took hold in their hearts. Yet, despite her alliances, Mheava herself never bowed to Chaos. She viewed them as usurper gods, just more intruders looking to take land belonging to gods her people had worshipped for generations. This defiance became her undoing, for her lieutenants had no such scruples. Following whispered promises, they ambushed Mheava, taking her crown for their own. 

Mheava was laid to rest in an enormous burial mound. Here, her lieutenants hoped, her soul would be held until the End Times came, trapped by the strongest magic known to both Human and Beastman. And inside she stayed, her spirit raging in its prison, even as her tribe fell to infighting and the Empire rose in their place. 

Centuries later, Old Jasper’s wandering took him past her barrow. He carried with him fresh magic, enough to let her spirit clamber back into her desiccated remains. Now a Wight of ancient and terrible power, she smashed aside the enchantments imprisoning her and emerged into a world changed, with only the miserable Liche and his Corpse Cart where once she had legions of loyal followers. 

Mheava now serves as Jasper’s defender and servant. She is bound to him by the magic keeping her body intact, and knows that if Jasper were to fall, she might eventually return to true death. However, her will remains as strong as it did in life and she rails against this prison as much as she did her tomb. She will serve Jasper, for now. But she is always on the lookout for a chance, her moment to reclaim her rightful rule. The land is hers. The people in it hers. Their dead are hers! And one day Jasper will learn Mheava is no one’s puppet.

## **The Herald Wight**
Before the Night Parade arrive in a settlement, a figure in ragged motley appears. They dance down the road, limbs moving like a puppet cut free of its strings. Ancient bells jingle, and every movement is accompanied by a rhythmic snap and crack. Sometimes, the figure attracts a train of eager children, following them to find where the performance is to be. Sooner or later, they reach the town’s centre, and here their true nature becomes clear. 

The wide brim of their hat is pushed back to reveal a skeletal grin. Eyes burning with Morrslieb’s light look out from a face stripped clean of flesh. Then they bow, extend their hand, and deliver their ultimatum: ‘Bring out your dead.’ 

This Wight has become known as the Herald. The Night Parade are never far behind them and they are sometimes to be sighted dancing at the Parade’s head, their strange, jerking movements making them stand out from the rest of that shuffling company. They never speak, beyond delivering their message, and they never stop dancing, holding out their hand to passers-by, inviting them to join in. There are plenty of stories about those who accept, and even more about those who refuse. 

The Herald does not always dance alone. Sometimes they appear amidst a town’s graveyard, the dead clawing their way up to join them. These they lead around town in a grotesque morris dance, a sight of which has been known to empty settlements overnight, families leaving their dead to the Night Parade’s predations. 

On occasion, villagers do stand against them. The Herald has been reported destroyed countless times over the decades, mobbed by those eager to stave off the coming evil. Yet it is never long before they are sighted again, stretching out their hand to the next settlement in the Night Parade’s path. 

## **The Charnel Chorus Mass Grave Dead**
Most Undead risen from mass graves do not last long. Usually, they are nothing more than a byproduct of a necromancer’s summoning, destined to collapse upon themselves within mere hours. The Charnel Chorus is an exception. 

This collection of yellowing, cracked skulls follows the Night Parade wherever it journeys, borne aloft by a tide of shifting bones, serpentine spines, and spider-like ribs. Always the skulls keep up their crackling song, chanting dirges to Morr in eternal mockery. 

Jasper summoned the Charnel Chorus from an ossuary outside Schrabwald. The small chapel dedicated to the god of the dead had been a resting place for his devotees for generations, their bones decorating its walls and their skulls watching over his worshippers. 

Over the years, though, the chapel was abandoned, reclaimed by the Reikwald Forest. Morr’s protection faded, and the chapel slowly became nothing more than a local curiosity, a place where scholars from Altdorf muttered about architecture and children dared one another to spend the night. Until the skulls heard the clang of Jasper’s bell. 

Jasper seems to take delight in maintaining the Chorus long past the point where it should have collapsed. Its skulls turn up on the walls of towns he intends to plunder, singing to the defenders and sapping their will to fight. Sometimes Jasper decorates his cart with them, providing himself with a further defence should the need arise. 

Morr’s priests and templars take the creature as a particular insult to their order. Many among the Black Guard have sworn to end the Chorus’s song, or die in the attempt. So far, none have succeeded. Always some part escapes, reforming and regrowing before seeking their revenge. Among the Chorus’s many skulls, there now sing more than a few once belonging to those who hunt the Undead.

## **It Tolls for Thee** Adventure Hooks Concerning the Night Parade
## Morbid Interest
Scholars Ernholt Weiss and Eirik Morklenburg have been studying the Undead in the hope they might be able to find a pattern to their behaviour. Such knowledge could be invaluable in protecting the Empire, or so they claim. During a recent analysis of local folklore, they encountered stories about the Night Parade, and became particularly fascinated with the figure known as the Herald. 

The two scholars believe the Herald’s strange mannerisms mark them as unique among the Undead, and have a theory they might represent a new path forward in their studies. A dual crescent moon is due to happen soon, traditionally the time when the Night Parade make their rounds. If the Characters could capture the Herald, and avoid the attention of Morr’s Black Guard as they transport them back to Altdorf, the scholars would pay handsomely. 

Both lords declared this to be a heinous act of desecration by their foe, and fresh conflict has broken out, with neither allowing anyone time to step foot on to the battlefield to recover their dead. 

Agatha Haas, a priest who tends a local shrine honouring all the gods, has begged the two generals to let the dead be given their proper rest. She even tried telling them the Night Parade have been sighted nearby, and they are most likely the reason for their missing dead. Both scoffed at such superstitions and are already making plans for the next attack. 

Desperate to stop the Undead from claiming any more of her parishioners, Agatha comes to the Characters for help. Either the generals must be made to see sense, or the battlefield must be cleared of corpses, tonight. Already, huntsmen have heard the sound of a bell making its way back to the killing ground. If they don’t act soon, this conflict will drown the land in its dead. 

## My Will Be Done
Matteo De Spaza, a wizard of the Amethyst order, has come to the Grey Mountains in order to stamp out the Night Parade. He has a plan to disrupt the magic empowering them, leaving the Undead vulnerable. 

An arcane artefact recently came into his possession: a small, black box originating in distant Lustria. By focussing one’s mind to its patterns, the box can be opened and will swallow the winds of magic into itself for a time. If the Characters could plant this device in Jasper’s Corpse Cart somehow, the magic binding the Undead would be momentarily broken, leaving them directionless and easy to pick off. 

However, De Spaza is secretly a necromancer himself and sees in the Night Parade an opportunity to claim power. If he can disrupt the Liche’s magic, he believes he could bind him to his own will, leading him to wherever he hides away the legions of Undead. 

## A Likely Story
While they are resting in a tavern, the Characters’ quiet drink is interrupted when a wild-eyed traveller bursts in. Without a word to anyone, she strides over to the bar and begins begging for ale. Eventually, she calms down enough to relate her tale. 

A pedlar by trade, she camped down for the night by the roadside, drinking from her flask of spirits to keep herself warm. And then another drink to keep her spirits up. And another just for something to do. The next thing she knew, she was in a cart, lying atop a pile of corpses. At first, she thought some corpse collector had mistaken her for dead. Then she heard the corpses moaning, felt the limbs beneath her move, and looked up at the hooded and cloaked figure whose eyes burned with corpse fire. She doesn’t know how long she lay there, pretending to be dead. At last, the cart stopped moving and she took her chance, running as fast as she could and not stopping until she found the tavern’s lights. 

## Alike in Villainy
Two noble houses are at war over a disputed border, an argument which has already cost many lives down the centuries. However, the bodies from their most recent battle have all disappeared. 

While none believe her, the peddlar has, by sheer luck, survived an encounter with the Night Parade. Jasper is loath to give up any he claims. Even as the peddlar is dragged away to the lock-up for making a public nuisance, the Herald is making their way towards the settlement, the Parade not far behind them. 

## **Encounters with the Night Parade**
The strength of the Night Parade varies depending on how long they have been travelling and how many dead they have gathered. Their entirety may be too much for inexperienced adventurers, while dealing only with stragglers could be far too simple a matter for more experienced Characters. 

Below are three different examples in which the Characters might encounter only a portion of the Parade. When planning your adventure, choose the most appropriate for your group, or feel free to tailor the Parade for a greater, or lesser, challenge. 

## **Mop Up the Stragglers Easy Encounter**
Jasper’s command over the dead is not always perfect, and wherever his Corpse Cart travels dark magic lingers. The Parade leave a trail of the dead wherever they pass, who have either wandered off from their main body, or who are newly risen by the magic staining the ground wherever the Parade go. These can form new bands of wandering Undead, aimless save for their need to kill, and soon to be mopped up by either those who hunt such creatures, or the Night Parade when they retrace their path back to the Grey Mountains. 

There are two main situations in which adventurers might encounter such groups: 

The first is when those Undead who were following Jasper fell behind due to some delay or Jasper’s lessening control over the Parade’s growing numbers. If something were to happen to Old Jasper, much of the Night Parade would break apart into such groups. They might still be following the direction the Corpse Cart went, or they may stay where they are. Lesser Undead, such as Zombies and Skeletons, rarely have their own goals or aims, though some may still have some lingering concept of where they once lived and try to return there. They attack anything that gets too close. 

The second is when those dead who did not rise when the Night Parade passed nonetheless felt its call. Perhaps it took them longer to free themselves from their graves, or they died shortly after the Night Parade passed by. Either way, the dark magic left in the Parade’s wake can still be enough to animate them, meaning settlements deal with sporadic outbursts of the Undead days after the Night Parade has moved on. 

There is no set make-up for a gang of stragglers, but it will normally be comprised of lesser Undead, such as Zombies and Skeletons, ones without a will of their own to direct them. Larger, slower creatures, such as Mass Grave Dead, often accompany such bands, though their integrity rarely lasts long. 

Encountering stragglers is rarely challenging for adventurers: they are few in number and are working entirely on instinct, without any organised direction or tactics. However, if they are not dealt with soon, their numbers will start to increase. The more they kill, the more dark magic gathers around them, raising their victims in turn. 

A group of stragglers may consist of: 

- Five Zombies clustered together. 

His control over the Undead is also at its strongest during this time, and he is able to direct their efforts with greater efficacy. The result of this is that, rather than wandering or attacking aimlessly, the dead display greater unity of purpose, and even fundamental tactics according to Jasper’s instructions. 

During this time, Jasper is primarily concerned with gathering corpses and growing his numbers. He therefore prioritises places where he is sure to find a rich supply. The ill-defended burial gardens, which are kept by most hamlets, battlefields, and charnel pits are his main objectives. 

- Two Skeletons. 

A Bring Out Your Dead group might consist of: 

- One rotten steed or one Zombie Mass Grave Dead. 

## **Bring Out Your Dead Medium Encounter**
When the Night Parade first set out, their numbers are relatively few. There are always some dead for them to pick up, those unfortunates left unburied, victims to bandits or monsters, and dead forest creatures also find themselves drawn to the bell’s call. Yet, at this stage, the Parade is more elite, clustered tightly around Jasper and his cart. 

To make up for their lack of numbers, Jasper is more cautious. The Herald goes ahead, putting out the call for corpses and testing a settlement’s defences. Should the Herald be destroyed, Jasper takes the Parade elsewhere, raising another Skeleton to the Wight’s former status. 

Unable to rely upon the Night Parade’s numbers to protect himself, Jasper keeps Mheava and the other Wights close. 

- The Herald and six Zombies, about a mile ahead of the main force. 

- Left flank: lesser Undead about half a mile from Jasper, consisting of three Dire Wolves, five Zombies, and a Skeleton. 

- Right flank: lesser Undead about half a mile from Jasper, consisting of three Skeletons, two Zombies, and one Zombie Demigryph. 

- A command corps consisting of Old Jasper (Corpse Cartmounted Liche), four Wights, Mheava, two Skeletons, and four Zombies. 

- The Charnel Chorus may appear at any position in the Night Parade. 

## **Danse Macabre Hard Encounter**
In this scenario, Old Jasper has successfully gathered his full complement of Undead and is set to return to the Grey Mountains. This is the last chance for anyone looking to end the old Liche before he will be inaccessible in whatever hold he delivers the dead to. This is also when Jasper is at his most dangerous. The Parade, by this time, has swollen in size, with Undead wandering up to half a mile around its centre. Settlements now hold little interest to Jasper, but their inhabitants are likely to be swept up in the Parade’s path if they don’t take measures to get out of their way. Despite this, there are some key weaknesses Characters may be able to exploit. 

Due to the Parade’s increased size, Jasper no longer has fine control over its numbers. The further they are away from Jasper, the more likely they are to be easily distracted and wander off, eventually forming groups of stragglers. Observing the Parade could show that some of the Undead are no longer moving with the same unity of purpose, and are breaking away from their fellows to chase sounds or animals. Characters could use this to try to disperse the Undead further, or make themselves a path to its centre where Old Jasper lies. 

Old Jasper is vulnerable during this time. In order to maintain the Parade’s cohesion, he must send Mheava, the Herald, and the other Wights to the outer limits, relying on the Parade’s increased size to prevent enemies from reaching him. Taking out Jasper may not end the Undead threat all at once. Some lesser Undead may collapse, but most would form groups of stragglers. Mheava would take back her own will, claiming whatever power she can from Jasper’s remains before taking her Wights into the forest to plot her revenge against whatever power he served. Even without killing Jasper, sending Mheava away means his command over her is weakened. While Mheava may not be able to talk, and would not be able to disobey Jasper directly, she would not be above communicating with those who could end him. 

The full Night Parade consist of: 

- Mheava (Skeletal Steed-mounted Wight Champion) with two Skeleton cavalry (skeletal steed-mounted Skeletons), three Skeletons, and four Zombies, about a mile ahead of the main force. 

- Left flank: lesser Undead, half a mile from Jasper, consisting of one Wight, two Dire Wolves, and seven Zombies. 

- Right flank: lesser Undead, half a mile from Jasper, consisting of one Wight, four Skeletons, two Dire Wolves, and one Zombie Demigryph. 

- A command corps consisting of Old Jasper (Corpse Cartmounted Liche), two Wights, two Skeletons, and four Zombies. 

- The rear, up to a mile from Jasper, consisting of five Zombiess and a Mass Grave Dead. 

- The Herald (rotten steed-mounted Wight) moves around the Parade’s edges, corralling stragglers. 

- The Charnel Chorus will either be found at the rear (replacing the usual Mass Grave Dead, if there was one), or on Old Jasper’s Corpse Cart if he feels threatened. 

Finally, this is when the Night Parade are the most difficult to dismiss as a threat. The Characters will have an easier time assembling allies to stand against it, though a head-on attack could prove disastrous for all involved. 

## **Corpse Carts**
Hideous amalgamations of dead flesh and rotting wood, Corpse Carts have plagued the Old World since hapless corpse collectors became bound to their charges as warpstone rained over Sylvania. Pulled by pitiful Zombies, bells tolling in time with their cargo’s moaning cries, these Undead constructs act as dark magic wellsprings, filling the dead with unnatural life. 

Corpse Carts can be found wandering roads and byways throughout the Empire. They are often sought by necromancers looking to enhance their powers. Some necromancers even try making their own, carrying out sickening rituals to fuse man, beast, and cart together, which they then use as mounts. They are not alone in hunting them, though. The Black Guard of Morr take reports of Corpse Carts very seriously. Sightings of such a construct nearby is one of the few times these dour templars may leave their station guarding the Gardens of Morr. 

Corpse Carts quickly enter local lore, with tales of them being shared around the fire on a dark Geheimnisnacht. It is rare to find a region without its own variation, populating the roads with sinister Night Parades, garish Charnavals, or the mournful fiddle of the Totentanz. This can be put down to the fact that no two Corpse Carts are ever alike. They all carry something to call the dead from Morr’s silent kingdom, whether it be a bell or the driver’s mournful keening, but aside from that they vary greatly in form and origin. 

Some Corpse Carts are left loose when their necromantic creators are hunted down, or the armies they marched in suffer defeat. Others are the product of accidents, plague carts twisted together with the corpses they carry after coming into contact with warpstone or other strange magics. Whatever they owe their origins to, the effect is the same. Wherever a Corpse Cart passes, the dead sleep lightly.

## **Vigor Mortis**
Any Undead within 8 of the Corpse Cart are no longer subject to the _Unstable_ rule. The Corpse Cart itself continues to be subject to this, reflecting the dangerous nature of the magic it holds. 

In addition, any attempt to cast a spell from the Lore of Necromancy within 8 of the Corpse Cart is made at +20. 

These effects end should the Corpse Cart be destroyed. 

## Balefire Brazier
Instead of a bell, some Corpse Carts carry a Balefire Brazier. These warpstone torches burn with witchlight, consuming the winds of magic and forcing all Lore (Magic) checks made within 8 of them to suffer a -20 penalty. 

This replaces the usual benefit the cart provides to Lore of Necromancy spellcasting. 

## The Lost and the Damned
Corpse Carts may originate anywhere bodies need to be transported from one place to the next. Rural settings are their most common haunts, as many settlements are quite some distance from the nearest Garden of Morr, relying instead on either passing corpse collectors or their own less well-defended graveyards. Cities are just as reliant upon corpse collectors, especially in times of plague, and it is not unknown for these constructs to appear wandering their streets. There have even been reports of barges laden with bloated dead, clawing their way along rivers. 

It is not just human dead who are vulnerable. Dwarf families, for example, pay extravagant sums to have their remains returned to their ancestral holds. Any such procession has the potential to become a Corpse Cart, given the right circumstance, and guards are hired to ensure the dearly departed are defended in their final journey. 

**Traits:** Armour 3, Construct, Constrictor, Corrupted (2), Dark Vision, Die Hard, Fear 3, Painless, Rear, Size (Large), Undead, Unstable, 5 x Flailing Limbs+7 **Optional:** Balefire Brazier, Diseased, Distracting, Infected, Infestation, Trained (Mount) 

## **Jasper Has a Bone or Two to Pick...**
## Body Check
Smuggler Igor Sirren has been tasked by his client, a mysterious but influential individual in Altdorf, to bring some… sensitive possessions down from the north. In particular, she wants to make sure a Khemrian artefact she’s been studying arrives without issue. 

## Never Truly Gone
Every year, a Corpse Cart passes through Stirasholm. The adventurers overhear the villagers talking about it, yet there is no horror in their voices. The place appears to be preparing for a celebration. Bunting is hung as the villagers get ready to welcome their loved ones back. 

Knowing the superstitions held by the Empire’s common folk, Igor has a foolproof plan to ensure they won’t look too closely. All it takes is one ramshackle cart, a pile of corpses, and some people looking for quick coin to pretend to be Zombies. 

Igor is sure that, with the Characters’ help, they’ll pull off this masquerade without issue. No one who knows the story of the Corpse Carts will want to hang around when they hear one coming, and even if they did, who’s going to dig through a pile of bodies for one measly stone scroll case? 

That night, the cart arrives: a tattered thing, dragging behind it a group of Zombies. They don’t pay the villagers, who lean out their windows and throw flowers as they walk past, any heed. Some villagers are in tears, reaching out to loved ones. The dead never look at them, until a man stumbles into their path, begging for his daughter to return. 

## Collect Them All
While enjoying an Altdorf market day, the adventurers bear witness to a disgusting sight. Someone screams, people turn and flee, crushing stalls and one another in their panic. Out from the mess stumbles a monster. Flesh stretches over a wooden frame; legs twitch beside shattered wheels; the whole thing dragged by one, misshapen creature, bloody tears running from ruined eye sockets. The thing manages five more steps before it collapses under its own weight. 

A few moments later, a woman dressed in a black cuirass and wielding a greatsword arrives at the scene. She calls herself Sister Umbra, a templar dedicated to Morr. Recently, the temple of Morr has been losing acolytes sent out as corpse collectors, only for them to turn up like this. She believes a necromancer is seeking to make a Corpse Cart, something she has heard about in stories from the old Vampire Wars. Anything the Characters saw could be the key!
